answer: A nebula of agents can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to earn trust through verifiable useful work before it gains any privileges: every newcomer must tend a small orchard of real tasks — answering queries, checking data, running jobs — with its output sampled and scored by peers. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand orchards of real compute, while a bridge of portable reputation lets honest agents carry their proven history across services instead of starting from zero each time.
